{{nihongo|'''Kureha-Anekurahime Shrine'''|姉倉比売神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Etchū Province]].

It is also written as '''Anekura-hime Shrine'''. The shrine is built atop an ancient burial mound (kofun).

There are two shrines of the same name within Toyama City ({{ill|Kureha-hime origin shrine|ja|呉羽町 (富山市)|qid=Q86731852|lt=Kureha-hime origin shrine}} and Funakura). Both are considered candidate shrines (ronsha) of the {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} “Anekurahime Shrine of {{ill|Etchū Province|ckb|پارێزگای ئێتچو|cs|Provincie Eččú|de|Provinz Etchū|es|Provincia de Etchū|fa|ولایت اتچو|fr|Province d'Etchū|gl|Provincia de Etchū|id|Provinsi Etchū|it|Etchū|ja|越中国|ko|엣추국|lt|Ečiū žemė|nl|Etchu (provincie)|pt|Província de Etchū|ru|Эттю (провинция)|simple|Etchū Province|sk|Eččú (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечу|tr|Etchū (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Еттю|vi|Tỉnh Etchū|zh|越中國|zh_min_nan|Ettyû-kok|zh_yue|越中國|qid=Q906899}}, {{ill|Nei District, Toyama|ja|婦負郡|ko|네이군|zh|婦負郡|qid=Q6987940}}.” Both formerly held the rank of {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
The {{ill|Saijin|abstract|Q11591100|fr|Saijin|ja|祭神|zh|祭神|qid=Q11591100}} is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Anekurahime-no-Kami}}. According to a synthesis of the shrine traditions of both shrines, Anekurahime-no-Kami subdued bandits in the region, established her residence on Mount Funakura, ruled the area, and spread agriculture, sericulture, and weaving among the local people. In the “Sentatsuroku,” Anekurahime-no-Kami was married to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Isurugi-hiko-no-Kami}} of Noto (the enshrined deity of {{ill|Isurugi Hikojinja|ja|伊須流岐比古神社|qid=Q11381009}}). However, Isurugi-hiko-no-Kami entered into a relationship with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Noto-hime-no-Kami}} of Mount Senbokuyama (the enshrined deity of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Noto-hime Shrine}}). Enraged, Anekurahime-no-Kami hurled stones from Mount Funakura to attack Noto-hime-no-Kami. Anekurahime-no-Kami’s younger sister, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Fukurahime-no-Kami}}, also joined the attack, plunging the land of Koshi into great turmoil. {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}} of Izumo was dispatched to Koshi by order of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takami-musubi-no-Kami}}, and together with five assembled deities, he suppressed the rebellion. As punishment for causing the disturbance, Anekurahime-no-Kami was stripped of her territory and exiled to Kureha Kotake, where she was ordered to teach weaving to the local women. Fukurahime-no-Kami received the same punishment. Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto and the others then attacked the remaining two deities and ultimately executed Isurugi-hiko-no-Kami and Noto-hime-no-Kami on the seashore.

The place name “Nei District” (婦負郡) is derived from Anekurahime-no-Kami, and the place name “Kureha” is also associated with weaving.

At the Kureha Anekurahime Shrine, {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto}} are additionally enshrined as principal deities<ref name="p111" />.

=== Overview ===
;Kureha-hime origin shrine
*Location – 1813 Kureha Town, Toyama City, Toyama Prefecture<ref name="p111">“Toyama Prefecture Shrine Gazetteer” (November 10, 1983), edited and published by the Toyama Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines, p. 111.</ref>.
*Shrine grounds – 3,950 tsubo (formerly located on a keyhole-shaped tumulus)<ref name="p111" />

:It is said to be the oldest shrine in Etchū Province<ref name="p111" />. Nearby, it served as a base for {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|Q311080|qid=Q311080}}’s march to the capital ({{ill|Joraku|Q10867576|qid=Q10867576}}). In {{ill|1537|Q6461|qid=Q6461}} ({{ill|Genbun|Q1145754|qid=Q1145754}} 7), 200 koku of shrine lands were donated, and on {{ill|February 26|Q2359|qid=Q2359}}, {{ill|1546|Q6533|qid=Q6533}} ({{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} 7), a written prayer was dedicated to the shrine. On {{ill|July 17|Q2729|qid=Q2729}}, {{ill|1721|Q6913|qid=Q6913}} ({{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 5), the Tanaka Shrine was transferred and jointly enshrined. In {{ill|1870|Q7741|qid=Q7741}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 3), the main hall was rebuilt, and on {{ill|May 11|Q2558|qid=Q2558}}, {{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}} (Meiji 9), the Shinmei Shrine was transferred and jointly enshrined. In {{ill|1897|Q7847|qid=Q7847}} (Meiji 30), the shrine buildings were rebuilt. In {{ill|1955|Q18577|qid=Q18577}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 30), a new protective roof over the sanctuary was constructed, and in {{ill|1978|Q2483|qid=Q2483}} (Shōwa 53), the worship hall underwent major repairs. (“Toyama Prefecture Shrine Gazetteer,” p. 112.)

;Funakura
*Location – 2360 Funakura, Toyama City, Toyama Prefecture<ref name="p157">“Toyama Prefecture Shrine Gazetteer” (November 10, 1983), edited and published by the Toyama Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines, p. 157.</ref>.
*Shrine grounds – 13,157 tsubo<ref name="p157" />

:Founded during the {{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269}} (when the monk Kifuku established the Shingon Buddhist temple Jōryū-ji). After Jōryū-ji burned down during the {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} era, the shrine is said to have been established on its former site.
